insights.title: Mortgages are the riskiest product and also 52% of exposure
insights.so_what: Mortgage default rate is 24.7% vs 16.1% for the portfolio and 13.9% for Auto Loan. Because it carries 52% of exposure, a few points of extra default here matter more than any other product. Secured does not mean safe: review underwriting and collateral valuation on this book first.

insights.title: Default risk falls steadily with income: 39% below 30k vs 8% above 120k
insights.so_what: Customers earning under 60k are 22% of accounts but 34% of defaults. Age follows the same pattern (22.4% under 25 vs 10.6% at 55+). Affordability checks and lower limits for low-income, young applicants are the cheapest lever.

insights.title: Unemployed customers default at 35%, about 2.3x salaried
insights.so_what: The segment is only 4.9% of exposure but is the sharpest single risk marker (718 accounts). Other employment types sit within a narrow band (13.6% to 17.3%), so a decline or manual-review rule for this segment is easy to target without penalising everyone else.

insights.title: Cross-cut: Unemployed Credit Card holders default at 39% (n=197)
insights.so_what: The worst cell with at least 100 accounts is Unemployed x Credit Card at 38.6% (2.4x the portfolio rate). Separately, Mortgage default stays between 20.2% and 27.2% even for employed groups, so its risk is a product effect, not just an unemployment effect. Use the pair, not either dimension alone, for limit setting.

insights.title: A missed payment in the first 3 months lifts default risk from 15% to 22%
insights.so_what: 1,905 accounts (13.0%) missed at least one of their first three payments and default at 21.5% vs 15.3%. Accounts that never miss in 12 months default at 12.9%. An early-collections trigger at month 3 reaches the riskiest accounts while there is still time to restructure.
